title: The Missing Lunchbox
content: Have you ever noticed that some children don't bring a lunchbox to school? They eat their meals in a big dining hall with all their friends. Let's find out why!

title: What Do You Think?
content: What would it be like to live at your school day and night? How would meal times be different from eating at home?

content.title: A Boarding School Dining Hall
content.description: Imagine a huge hall with long tables where hundreds of students eat together.

title: Life in a Boarding School
content: In a boarding school, students live and study together. They eat all their meals in a large common dining hall. It's like having a big family meal every day!

definition: A school where students reside during the semester.

question: Where do students eat their meals in a boarding school?

title: Reflect on Sharing
content: If you had to share a room and all your meals with 50 other students, what would be the most fun part? What would be difficult?

title: Connecting to Community
content: Eating together builds strong friendships, just like how families bond over dinner at home. Sharing food is a beautiful way to show you care.

title: Plan a Class Picnic
content: Plan a special meal where everyone in your class brings one item, and you all share and eat together like a big family!
Encourage students to share their experiences of eating at large gatherings like weddings or festivals.

title: The Mystery of the Mega Kitchen
content: Imagine a kitchen that never closes, where anyone can walk in and get a free hot meal, no matter who they are. Does such a place exist?

title: What Do You Think?
content: Imagine you have to cook for 1,000 people today! How would you do it? Who would chop the vegetables? Where would you get such huge pots?

content.title: A Giant Kitchen at the Gurudwara
content.description: Look at the enormous utensils used for cooking large quantities of food.

title: Langar - The Community Kitchen
content: This mega kitchen is real! It happens every day in a Gurudwara. The free meal served to everyone, sitting together on the floor, is called Langar. It teaches us equality, humility, and the joy of serving others (Seva).

definition: The community kitchen in a Gurudwara where a free meal is served to all visitors, without distinction.
A place of assembly and worship for Sikhs.

question: What is the free meal served in a Gurudwara called?

content: Some might think Langar is only for a specific religion, but it is open to all human beings regardless of religion, caste, or background.

title: Think About It
content: Why do you think people of all backgrounds sit together on the floor to eat in a Langar? How does it make everyone feel equal?

title: Connecting the Dots
content: Langar is a perfect example of teamwork and community service. Just like ants work together to build a colony, humans work together to feed thousands! Cooking and eating together brings harmony.

title: Be a Master Chef Helper
content: Next time you attend a community gathering or a Langar, observe the large utensils used and try to help with simple tasks like serving water or picking up plates!
